title: IS 269:2015 — Ordinary Portland Cement — Specification (Sixth Revision)
content: Scope: This standard covers the manufacture and chemical and physical requirements of 33 grade, 43 grade and 53 grade ordinary Portland cement. Portland cement is designated as OPC 33, OPC 43 and OPC 53 according to the 28-day compressive strength.

title: IS 269:2015 — Ordinary Portland Cement — Specification (Sixth Revision)
content: Compressive Strength Requirements: The compressive strength of mortar cubes prepared in accordance with IS 4031 (Part 6) shall not be less than: for 33 Grade: 16 MPa (72h), 22 MPa (168h), 33 MPa (672h/28 days); for 43 Grade: 23 MPa (72h), 33 MPa (168h), 43 MPa (28 days); for 53 Grade: 27 MPa (72h), 37 MPa (168h), 53 MPa (28 days).

title: IS 269:2015 — Ordinary Portland Cement — Specification (Sixth Revision)
content: Physical Requirements: Initial setting time shall not be less than 30 minutes. Final setting time shall not be more than 600 minutes when tested according to IS 4031 (Part 5). Soundness by Le Chatelier method shall not exceed 10 mm and by autoclave expansion shall not exceed 0.8 percent.

title: IS 269:2015 — Ordinary Portland Cement — Specification (Sixth Revision)
content: Chemical Requirements: Insoluble residue shall not exceed 5.0 percent by mass. Magnesia (MgO) content shall not exceed 6.0 percent. Total loss on ignition (LOI) shall not exceed 5.0 percent. Total sulphur content calculated as sulphuric anhydride (SO3) shall not exceed 3.5 percent.

title: IS 269:2015 — Ordinary Portland Cement — Specification (Sixth Revision)
content: Marking and Mandatory Certification: Under the Cement (Quality Control) Order notified by Ministry of Commerce and Industry, all cement manufactured or sold in India must mandatorily conform to IS 269 and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under Scheme I of BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations.

title: IS 374:2019 — Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Specification (Fourth Revision)
content: Scope: This standard specifies the mechanical, electrical, performance and safety requirements of AC ceiling fans including BLDC (Brushless Direct Current) ceiling fans operating on single phase supply up to 250V.

title: IS 374:2019 — Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Specification (Fourth Revision)
content: Air Delivery and Service Value: For 1200 mm sweep ceiling fans, minimum air delivery shall not be less than 210 cubic metres per minute (m3/min). Minimum service value (air delivery per watt) shall conform to Star rating requirements defined under Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) standards.

title: IS 374:2019 — Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Specification (Fourth Revision)
content: Electrical Safety and Insulation: The insulation resistance measured between live parts and the frame shall not be less than 2 Megaohms when tested with a 500V DC megger. Electric fans must withstand high voltage dielectric test of 1500V AC for one minute without breakdown.

title: IS 374:2019 — Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Specification (Fourth Revision)
content: Mandatory Certification: Under the Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, ceiling fans require mandatory BIS certification with ISI mark under Scheme I. Manufacturers must maintain an in-house laboratory to perform routine tests including high voltage test and air delivery test.

title: IS 14543:2024 — Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) — Specification
content: Definition and Processing: Packaged drinking water means water derived from any source of potable water subjected to treatments like decantation, filtration, micron filtration, activated carbon filtration, demineralisation, reverse osmosis, and disinfection by UV irradiation or ozonisation.

title: IS 14543:2024 — Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) — Specification
content: Microbiological Requirements: The packaged drinking water shall be free from Escherichia coli (E. coli) in 250 ml, Coliform bacteria in 250 ml, Faecal streptococci in 250 ml, Pseudomonas aeruginosa in 250 ml, and Yeast and Mould in 250 ml. Total viable colony count shall not exceed 100 CFU/ml at 20°C-22°C.

title: IS 14543:2024 — Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) — Specification
content: Toxic and Chemical Limits: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) shall be between 75 mg/l and 500 mg/l. Lead (as Pb) max 0.01 mg/l, Arsenic (as As) max 0.01 mg/l, Cadmium max 0.003 mg/l, Nitrate max 45 mg/l. Individual pesticide residue shall not exceed 0.0001 mg/l and total pesticide residues shall not exceed 0.0005 mg/l.

title: IS 14543:2024 — Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) — Specification
content: Mandatory Certification and Packaging: Under Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations and BIS Act, no person shall manufacture, pack or sell packaged drinking water without obtaining BIS Certification Mark (ISI Mark). Containers must be food grade PET/PC conforming to IS 15410 or IS 12252.

title: IS 1786:2008 — High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement — Specification
content: Scope: Covers requirements for deformed steel bars and wires for use as reinforcement in concrete in grades Fe 415, Fe 415D, Fe 500, Fe 500D, Fe 550, Fe 550D and Fe 600. The letter 'D' denotes higher elongation and ductility for earthquake-resistant design.

title: IS 1786:2008 — High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement — Specification
content: Chemical Composition Limits: For Fe 500D, maximum Carbon content is 0.25%, maximum Sulphur is 0.040%, maximum Phosphorus is 0.040%, and S+P combined is 0.075%. Carbon equivalent (CE) shall not exceed 0.42% for Fe 500D.

title: IS 1786:2008 — High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement — Specification
content: Mechanical Properties: For Fe 500D grade, minimum 0.2 percent proof stress/yield stress is 500 MPa. Minimum tensile strength (Rm) shall be at least 1.10 times the yield stress. Minimum percentage elongation on gauge length of 5.65√So is 16.0%.

title: IS 1786:2008 — High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement — Specification
content: Mandatory Steel Quality Control Order: Ministry of Steel notification mandates that all primary and secondary steel producers producing TMT bars must possess a valid BIS licence for IS 1786 with the ISI Mark.

title: IS 4151:2020 — Protective Helmets for Riders of Two Wheeled Motor Vehicles — Specification
content: Construction and Materials: A protective helmet consists of a rigid outer shell (ABS or polycarbonate), protective impact-absorbing liner (expanded polystyrene - EPS), comfort padding, and retention system (chin strap and buckle). Maximum helmet weight shall not exceed 1.2 kg.

title: IS 4151:2020 — Protective Helmets for Riders of Two Wheeled Motor Vehicles — Specification
content: Impact Attenuation Test: The helmet placed on an instrumented headform is dropped onto flat and kerbstone steel anvils at impact velocity of 7.5 m/s. The peak acceleration transferred to the headform shall not exceed 300g (gravitational units).

title: IS 4151:2020 — Protective Helmets for Riders of Two Wheeled Motor Vehicles — Specification
content: Retention System Dynamic Test: Chin strap dynamic displacement shall not exceed 35 mm under a 10 kg falling drop weight, and residual elongation shall not exceed 25 mm. The quick-release buckle shall open only with deliberate two-step action.

title: IS 4151:2020 — Protective Helmets for Riders of Two Wheeled Motor Vehicles — Specification
content: Mandatory Quality Control Order: Under Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) notification and BIS Helmet QCO, only helmets bearing the ISI mark conforming to IS 4151:2020 can be manufactured, imported or sold in India.

title: IS 1417:2016 — Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking
content: Standard Caratage and Fineness Grades: Gold jewellery hallmarking in India is permitted in 6 recognized grades: 24K (999 fineness, 99.9% pure), 23K (958 fineness, 95.8% pure), 22K (916 fineness, 91.6% pure), 20K (833 fineness, 83.3% pure), 18K (750 fineness, 75.0% pure), and 14K (585 fineness, 58.5% pure).

title: IS 1417:2016 — Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking
content: Mandatory Hallmarking Marks: Hallmarked gold jewellery must carry three distinct laser-etched marks: (1) BIS Logo (triangular mark), (2) Purity and Fineness mark (e.g. 22K916 or 18K750), (3) 6-digit alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification Number).

title: IS 1417:2016 — Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking
content: HUID Verification on BIS CARE App: Every hallmarked gold piece receives a unique 6-digit HUID at an authorized Assaying and Hallmarking Centre (AHC). Consumers can enter this HUID on the official 'BIS CARE' mobile app to verify the jeweller registration, AHC centre, hallmarking date, and purity grade.

title: IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 — Safety of Toys — Mechanical and Physical Properties
content: Small Parts and Choking Hazards: Toys intended for children under 36 months of age must not fit entirely within the small parts test cylinder (31.7 mm diameter by 57.1 mm depth) to prevent choking hazards.

title: IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 — Safety of Toys — Mechanical and Physical Properties
content: Heavy Metal Migration (Part 3): Heavy metal migration limits: Lead (Pb) max 90 mg/kg, Cadmium (Cd) max 75 mg/kg, Mercury (Hg) max 60 mg/kg, Arsenic (As) max 25 mg/kg, Barium (Ba) max 1000 mg/kg, Chromium (Cr) max 60 mg/kg.

title: IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 — Safety of Toys — Mechanical and Physical Properties
content: Toys (Quality Control) Order: DPIIT notification mandates compulsory BIS certification with ISI Mark under Scheme I for all toys manufactured in India or imported from abroad.

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations, 2018 — Scheme I (Product Certification / ISI Mark)
content: Procedure for Grant of Licence: Application is submitted online on Manakonline portal with Form I, application fee, test report from factory lab or recognized lab, and manufacturing infrastructure details. BIS officer conducts preliminary factory audit to verify manufacturing process, quality control staff, and testing equipment before granting licence.

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations, 2018 — Scheme I (Product Certification / ISI Mark)
content: Simplified Procedure for MSMEs: Under Option 2 (Simplified Procedure), MSMEs can obtain a licence within 30 days if they submit a satisfactory test report from a BIS-recognized laboratory along with an undertaking to comply with the Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT).

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations, 2018 — Scheme I (Product Certification / ISI Mark)
content: Surveillance and Market Sampling: Once a licence is granted, BIS conducts regular periodic unannounced surveillance audits of the factory and draws random market samples from retail stores to verify ongoing conformity to the standard.

title: Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) — Scheme II for Electronics and Information Technology Goods
content: Scope and Applicability: Under MeitY and MNRE orders, 64 product categories including Mobile Phones, Laptops, LED lamps, Smart TVs, Power banks, and Solar Inverters must be registered under CRS before sale in India.

title: Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) — Scheme II for Electronics and Information Technology Goods
content: Registration Process: Product samples are sent to a BIS-recognized test laboratory. Upon receiving a passing test report, the applicant submits an online registration on crsbis.in. Registration is granted with a unique R-number (e.g., R-XXXXXXXX) and Self-Declaration of Conformity mark.

title: BIS Consumer Services, BIS CARE App & Complaint Redressal Guide
content: BIS CARE Mobile App: Available on Google Play Store and Apple App Store. Allows consumers to: (1) Verify ISI Mark licence (CM/L number), (2) Verify CRS registration (R-number), (3) Verify Gold Hallmarking HUID, and (4) Register complaints against misuse of ISI mark or sub-standard products.

title: BIS Consumer Services, BIS CARE App & Complaint Redressal Guide
content: Consumer Grievance Redressal: If a consumer purchases an ISI marked or Hallmarked product that fails to meet BIS standards, they can file a grievance on the BIS portal or through BIS CARE app. BIS investigates and, if verified, orders product replacement, refund, or takes penal action under the BIS Act 2016.

title: IS 2347:2023 — Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Seventh Revision)
content: Scope and Capacity: Specifies requirements for domestic pressure cookers of nominal capacity up to and including 18 litres, intended for domestic cooking under pressure. Nominal operating gauge pressure shall not exceed 100 kPa (approx 1.0 kgf/cm²).

title: IS 2347:2023 — Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Seventh Revision)
content: Materials and Safety Construction: Body and lid shall be manufactured from food-grade aluminium alloy or stainless steel (AISI 304 or 316). Gaskets must be food-grade vulcanized rubber conforming to IS 7466. Handles must be insulated, flame-resistant phenolic moulding material per IS 1300.

title: IS 2347:2023 — Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Seventh Revision)
content: Mandatory Testing Requirements: (1) Operating Pressure Test: Operates smoothly at nominal working pressure of 1.0 kgf/cm² (100 kPa). (2) Proof Pressure Test: Every cooker must withstand internal hydrostatic test pressure of 2.0 kgf/cm² (twice operating pressure) without leakage or permanent distortion. (3) Bursting Pressure Test: Minimum burst pressure shall not be less than 3.0 kgf/cm² (three times operating pressure). (4) Safety Vent / Fusible Relief Device Test: Safety valve must release excess steam safely between 1.4 kgf/cm² and 1.8 kgf/cm² if vent tube gets blocked. (5) Handle Thermal Shock & Drop Test: Handles must withstand thermal cycling and drop tests without loosening or cracking.

title: IS 2347:2023 — Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Seventh Revision)
content: Mandatory Certification under QCO: Under the Domestic Pressure Cooker (Quality Control) Order, 2020 issued by DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all domestic pressure cookers manufactured, imported, stocked, or sold in India MUST mandatorily conform to IS 2347 and bear the BIS ISI Mark under Scheme I. Non-compliance is punishable under Section 29 of the BIS Act, 2016.

title: IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
content: Scope and Applications: Code of practice for general structural use of plain and reinforced concrete in buildings, bridges, foundations, slabs, beams, and columns across India.

title: IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
content: Constituent Materials: Cements permitted include OPC 33, 43, 53 grade (IS 269), Portland Pozzolana Cement (IS 1489), and Portland Slag Cement (IS 455). Reinforcement steel must be high strength deformed TMT bars conforming to IS 1786. Aggregates must conform to IS 383.

title: IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
content: Concrete Grades and Mix Proportioning: Concrete is graded by 28-day characteristic compressive strength: Ordinary concrete (M10, M15, M20), Standard concrete (M25, M30, M35, M40, M45, M50, M55), and High strength concrete (M60 to M80). Design mix per IS 10262 is mandatory for M25 and higher grades.

title: IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
content: Durability and Nominal Cover: Environmental exposure classified into 5 categories: Mild, Moderate, Severe, Very Severe, and Extreme. For RCC under moderate exposure, minimum cement content is 300 kg/m3 with maximum water-cement ratio 0.50. Minimum nominal cover to reinforcement: 20 mm for slabs, 25 mm for beams, 40 mm for columns, and 50 mm for footings.

title: IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
content: Structural Design Method: Design is based on the Limit State Method for Limit State of Collapse (flexure, compression, shear, and torsion) and Limit State of Serviceability (deflection and crack width limits). Partial safety factors: 1.5 for dead and live loads; 1.5 for concrete strength, and 1.15 for steel reinforcement.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 — Statutory Provisions & Quality Control Orders (QCO)
content: Power of Central Government to Direct Compulsory Use of Standard Mark: Under Section 16 of the BIS Act 2016, line ministries (DPIIT, Ministry of Steel, MeitY, Ministry of Power, etc.) notify Quality Control Orders (QCOs) in public interest or for human, animal, plant health, safety, and environmental protection. Once notified under a QCO, no person shall manufacture, import, distribute, sell, hire, lease, store or exhibit for sale any scheduled goods unless they conform to the relevant Indian Standard and bear the standard mark (ISI Mark under Scheme I or CRS under Scheme II) under a valid licence or certificate of conformity from BIS.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 — Statutory Provisions & Quality Control Orders (QCO)
content: Penalties for Violation of Quality Control Orders: Contravention of Section 16 or Section 17 of the BIS Act 2016 (such as manufacturing, importing, or selling goods under mandatory QCO without a valid BIS licence) is a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for a term up to two years, or with a fine which shall not be less than two lakh rupees and may extend up to five lakh rupees for the first contravention, and up to ten times the value of goods or articles produced for subsequent contraventions.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 — Statutory Provisions & Quality Control Orders (QCO)
content: Search and Seizure Powers: Authorised BIS inspecting officers have statutory power to enter premises, inspect manufacturing plants and retail shops, take samples, and seize goods bearing unauthorized or counterfeit ISI/CRS marks, or non-certified goods subject to mandatory QCOs.

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 — Scheme I (ISI Mark Product Certification)
content: Option 1 (Normal Procedure): The manufacturer applies online on Manakonline portal (manakonline.in), pays application fee. A BIS inspecting officer conducts an on-site factory verification audit to check manufacturing machinery, quality management, and in-house testing lab facilities. Samples are drawn and dispatched to a BIS recognized laboratory. Upon satisfactory test report and audit verification, the licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) is granted within 60 to 90 days.

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 — Scheme I (ISI Mark Product Certification)
content: Option 2 (Simplified Procedure): Designed for fast-track processing within 30 days. The applicant gets test samples tested in advance from a BIS-recognized or NABL accredited laboratory and submits the test report along with the application on Manakonline. The preliminary inspection is conducted by BIS within 15 days, and licence is granted within 30 days of application submission if in-house testing equipment and reports are satisfactory.

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 — Scheme I (ISI Mark Product Certification)
content: Concessions for MSMEs, Startups & Women Entrepreneurs: BIS provides significant financial relief under Scheme I: Micro enterprises and DPIIT-recognized Startups receive a 20% concession on application fee, annual licence fee, and minimum marking fee. Small enterprises receive a 10% concession. Women-led micro-enterprises and units located in North Eastern Region receive an additional special fee concession up to 50%.

title: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 — Scheme I (ISI Mark Product Certification)
content: Surveillance and Renewal: A BIS licence is initially valid for 1 or 2 years and can be renewed for up to 5 years via Manakonline upon payment of renewal and marking fees. BIS conducts continuous surveillance through periodic surprise factory audits and drawing random market samples to verify ongoing compliance with the Indian Standard.

title: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) — Guidelines & Guidelines for AIR
content: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) Overview: FMCS permits overseas manufacturing units outside India to obtain a BIS licence and use the ISI Standard Mark under Scheme I. Certification applies strictly to the manufacturing premises where production takes place, not to trading entities or importers.

title: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) — Guidelines & Guidelines for AIR
content: Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) Requirement: Every foreign manufacturer must nominate an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) resident in India who is an Indian citizen or an authorized executive of the manufacturer's registered Indian office or subsidiary. The AIR executes an indemnity bond and is legally responsible for fulfilling all provisions of the BIS Act, rules, and regulations on behalf of the foreign manufacturer.

title: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) — Guidelines & Guidelines for AIR
content: Inspection and Testing for FMCS: A physical factory audit is conducted at the overseas manufacturing site by a BIS officer to verify testing facilities and production lines. Sample products are sealed and tested at BIS-approved laboratories. Cost of travel, visa, per diem, and inspection charges are borne by the applicant. Average processing timeline is 3 to 6 months.

title: BIS Laboratory Network & Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
content: BIS In-house Laboratory Network: BIS operates a nationwide network of laboratories comprising the Central Laboratory (CL) at Sahibabad (Ghaziabad, UP), 5 Regional Laboratories: Western (WRL Mumbai), Southern (SRL Chennai), Eastern (ERL Kolkata), Northern (NRL Chandigarh/Mohali), and Central, along with 3 Branch Laboratories in Bengaluru, Patna, and Guwahati. Testing covers chemical, mechanical, electrical, electronics, microbiological, civil, and consumer goods.

title: BIS Laboratory Network & Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
content: Laboratory Recognition Scheme (LRS) & LIMS: Under the Laboratory Recognition Scheme (LRS), BIS recognizes over 300 NABL-accredited independent commercial, academic, and government laboratories across India to supplement in-house testing capacity. All sample registration, assignment, testing status, and digital test certificates are managed securely in real time through the central online portal LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System).
